intro.title: useMemo for Expensive Computation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that calculates and displays the factorial of a number. You will learn how to use the `useMemo` hook to optimize this expensive calculation, preventing it from re-running on every render. The core concept is memoization, which caches the result of a function call and only recalculates it when specific dependencies change. You will work with React's `useState` to manage the input number and `useMemo` to wrap the factorial function. This will help you understand how to improve performance in your React applications by avoiding unnecessary computations.
intro.usecase: In real applications, useMemo is essential for optimizing expensive calculations that would otherwise slow down interactive UI components. For example, data visualization dashboards often need to process large datasets to generate charts, graphs, or summary statistics when filters change. E-commerce product filters might perform complex sorting or price calculations on thousands of items as users adjust criteria. Without useMemo, these computations would run on every render, causing noticeable lag in user interactions like typing, filtering, or navigating between views.
